notes.meaning: Paul traveled along the inland roads through the high country of Asia Minor and arrived at Ephesus, keeping his earlier promise to return. Meanwhile, Apollos was preaching in Corinth, building on the foundation Paul had laid there. When Paul reached Ephesus, he met a small group of disciples whose knowledge of the Christian faith was still incomplete.

Paul noticed that something was missing in their spiritual life, so he asked if they had received the Holy Spirit when they believed. They replied that they had not even heard that the Holy Spirit was given. While they knew about God's Spirit from the Old Scriptures, they did not know that the Spirit had now been poured out on believers since Jesus rose and ascended.

Surprised by their reply, Paul asked what baptism they had received, since Christian baptism includes the name of the Holy Spirit. They answered that they had only received the baptism of John the Baptist. This showed that they had accepted John's call to turn from sin, but had not yet moved into the full life of the church.

Paul explained that John's baptism was focused on repentance, which means feeling true sorrow for sin and turning back to God. John had always told his hearers that his job was to prepare the way, and that they must put their trust in the One coming after him, who is Jesus. John was the messenger pointing forward, but Jesus is the Savior who actually gives new life.

After hearing Paul's explanation, these men gladly placed their faith in Jesus and were baptized into His name. This was not a needless repetition of baptism, but their very first Christian baptism, since John's ceremony had only pointed ahead to the Savior. By doing this, they publicly joined themselves to Christ and His kingdom.

Paul placed his hands on them in prayer, and the Holy Spirit came upon them with powerful, visible results. They began speaking in languages they had never learned and prophesying, which means speaking out God's truth with special boldness and insight. These gifts showed everyone that the same gospel that started in Jerusalem was now firmly established in Ephesus.

This whole group was made up of about twelve men. Though they had started out with very limited knowledge, God brought them into the full truth and used them as an early core for the church in Ephesus.

Paul followed his usual custom by going first to the Jewish synagogue, where he spoke boldly for three months. He reasoned with the people and tried to persuade them using the Scriptures, explaining how Jesus brings the kingdom of God, which is God's rightful rule over human hearts. The leaders listened to him far longer than people had in many other cities.

Some listeners in the synagogue became stubborn, refused to believe, and openly spoke evil of 'the Way,' which was an early name for the Christian faith. Seeing their hardened opposition, Paul withdrew from the synagogue and took the believers with him. He began holding daily discussions and teaching in the public lecture hall of a man named Tyrannus.

Paul continued teaching in this lecture hall every day for two full years. Because Ephesus was a major center for trade and travel, many visitors heard the gospel and carried it to neighboring towns and villages. As a result, almost everyone living in the province of Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the message about the Lord Jesus.

God chose to perform extraordinary miracles through Paul during this time in Ephesus. These signs went beyond the ordinary course of nature to capture the attention of a city deeply tangled in pagan magic and superstition.

People even carried cloths, such as work aprons and sweat-rags Paul used while laboring at his craft, and placed them on the sick. When these cloths touched the sick, physical diseases were healed and evil spirits left them. The cloths themselves had no magical power, but God graciously met people's simple faith to show that the healing came from Him alone.

Some traveling Jewish exorcists, who made their living going from town to town trying to drive out demons with spoken charms, attempted to use the name of Jesus. Seeing the power in Paul's ministry, they commanded a demon to leave by saying they bound it by the Jesus whom Paul preached. They treated the Savior's holy name like a lucky spell rather than placing personal faith in Him.

Among those doing this were the seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest. These young men had turned away from the sacred work of their family to wander about as superstitious fortune-tellers and conjurers for money.

The evil spirit spoke back through the possessed man, saying that it knew Jesus and recognized Paul, but had no idea who these men were. The demon knew the true authority of Christ and respected Paul as His servant, but it had no fear of pretenders who possessed no real relationship with God.

The man possessed by the evil spirit attacked the brothers with fierce, unnatural strength. He sprang upon them, overpowered all of them, and beat them so violently that they ran out into the street bleeding and with their clothes torn off.

News of this terrifying event quickly spread to all the Jews and Greeks living across Ephesus. A deep, reverent fear fell upon the whole city, because everyone realized that the name of Jesus was holy and could not be treated lightly. Because of this defeat of false exorcists, the name of the Lord Jesus was held in the highest honor.

Many people who had already believed were deeply stirred in their consciences and came forward to confess their sins. They openly revealed the dark, sinful practices and superstitious habits they had secretly kept from their past life.

Many people who had practiced sorcery brought their scrolls of magic formulas and burned them together in front of the whole public. When the value of the books was added up, the total came to fifty thousand silver coins, representing a huge fortune of many thousands of days of wages. By burning them rather than selling them, they broke completely with their old life and protected others from being led into sin.

In this powerful way, the word of the Lord continued to spread and win great victories in Ephesus. The gospel proved strong enough to overcome deep-seated superstitions, demonic opposition, and the greed of sinful businesses, genuinely transforming people's everyday lives.
